evidence.field: 字形解說; 字音及字義
evidence.text: The page labels a sequence oracle-bone, bronze, small-seal and standard script. Its account says the first three show a front-facing standing person and gives ‘adult’ as the original sense; it says the standard form is close to small seal. It separately gives modern Cantonese daai6 and Mandarin da4 for the large/opposite-small sense, and another Mandarin reading dai4 in 大夫. This is a source analysis, not a dated specimen or proof of a semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 — 大

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database analyzes 大 as a front-facing standing adult with arms hanging down. It proposes ‘adult’ relative to child as an original sense from which ‘big’ developed. It reports bronze 大 meaning ‘big’, opposite 小, citing 郘鐘「大鐘八聿(肆)」, and mentions use for 太 in some terms. It says early 大 and 夫 were one graph representing adult male and big; 夫 differentiated by adding a short stroke, considered by many scholars an embellishment. This is a specialist account, not an independently dated chain establishing the adult-to-big semantic link.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析：大

evidence.text: The file page describes 大-oracle.svg as a digital vector depiction in Shang oracle script style. It identifies source resources including the Academia Sinica database and gives a specific source image reference, 43.E628, on that database’s 大 page. The page describes the file as a modern digital vector, not a photograph of an ancient object, and states CC0/public-domain reuse.
evidence.title: File:大-oracle.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The page describes 大-seal.svg as a digital depiction of 大 in Shuowen seal-script style, with source resources including Sinica, Chinese Etymology and the CUHK database. It identifies a modern SVG file uploaded in 2017 and releases it under public-domain terms/CC0. It is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image.

evidence.text: Search result for 大-bronze.svg identifies it as a digital Western Zhou bronze-script character file and reports CC0 licensing/public-domain status. The file description is less complete in the opened search result than for the oracle and seal files; use as a candidate only with that provenance limitation.

evidence.source: CUHK database; source packet contains its earlier inspected Shuowen.org entry
evidence.field: graphic account and historical dictionary account
evidence.text: CUHK’s account rejects the popular outstretched-arms explanation in favor of arms hanging down. Shuowen’s traditional explanation that 大 depicts a human is an Eastern Han dictionary account, not independent confirmation of prehistoric formation. No new first-hand specimen inspection here settles anatomical details.

gaps: No component decomposition applies to standalone 大; the supported analysis treats the whole graph as an adult human pictograph. No sound component or whole-graph phonetic loan is proposed, so no component or object-name pronunciation comparison is needed.

The outstretched-arms explanation in local excerpts conflicts with the inspected CUHK description of arms hanging down. The education resource also describes a standing person but does not detail limb positions. No image pixels were inspected in this research stage.
No precisely dated earliest 大 oracle-bone specimen or dated use for ‘adult’ was established. CUHK cites a bronze inscription for ‘big’ but its exact vessel/date was not verified in this session.

The proposed adult-to-big semantic development is an explicit dictionary analysis; an independently dated sequence of intermediate senses was not collected. The 夫 relationship and the claim that its added stroke is decorative are source assertions, not a dated character-by-character derivation demonstrated here.

The broad oracle-bone-to-bronze-to-small-seal-to-standard sequence is supported as a sequence of labels, but detailed stroke changes, a specific corruption event, and chronology of variants remain unestablished.

The Academy Sinica source-image link cited by Wikimedia Commons (43.E628) could not be inspected as an individual record. The direct Wikimedia SVG retrieval failed due to unsupported image content type; Wikimedia description pages remain inspected and identify modern vector redrawings.

limitations.text: These are modern SVG redrawings based on cited or listed character-form resources, not photographs of ancient oracle bones, bronzes, or seal artifacts. The visual agent should verify rendered pixels and shape fit before final selection.

The bronze candidate’s exact source specimen and its date were not established from the inspected search result; treat ‘Western Zhou’ as the Commons style/category label rather than a verified date for a specific artifact.
